content.title: About
content.content: Cheese pizza is a popular fast‑food dish consisting of a dough base topped with tomato sauce and a generous layer of melted cheese. It is commonly served in fast‑food chains and pizzerias.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese layer can include mozzarella, cheddar, parmesan, or a blend of these.
The classic Italian Margherita pizza is considered the ancestor of the modern cheese pizza.
In the United States, cheese pizza ranks among the top‑5 best‑selling items in fast‑food menus.
Thick‑crust dough usually contains more yeast and a longer proofing time, making it puffier.
There is a “four‑cheese” variant that uses four different cheeses for a richer flavor.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese is rich in calcium, which supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The cheese topping provides a substantial amount of animal protein, aiding tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese contains vitamins B2 and B12, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Certain cheeses (e.g., mozzarella) contain live cultures that can benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat in cheese helps promote a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Cheese pizza can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consumption.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Cheese often contains a lot of salt, which can be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have allergic reactions to casein.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese pizza is typically eaten hot, sliced into wedges. Additional toppings such as fresh vegetables, olives, or herbs can be added to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to keep the crust crisp.
